title.zh: 卷340 列傳一百二十七 王杰 董诰 朱珪
title.en: Volume 340 Biographies 127: Wang Jie, Dong Gao, Zhu Gui
title.raw: 卷340 列傳一百二十七 王杰 董诰 朱珪

sentences.zh: 王杰，字偉人，陝西韓城人。

translations.literal: Wang Jie, style name Weiren, was a native of Hancheng in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie, whose courtesy name was Weiren, came from Hancheng in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 以拔貢考銓藍田教諭，未任，遭父喪，貧甚，為書記以養母。

translations.literal: As a selected tribute scholar he passed examination for the post of district tutor of Lantian but did not take office; he suffered his father's death, was very poor, and worked as a secretary to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a tribute scholar, he qualified in examination for the Lantian district tutorship but never took up the post. After his father's death left him destitute, he earned a living as a secretary to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 歷佐兩江總督尹繼善、江蘇巡撫陳宏謀幕，皆重之。

translations.literal: He successively served on the staffs of Liangjiang Governor-General Yin Jishan and Jiangsu Governor Chen Hongmou, and both held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn on the staffs of Liangjiang Governor-General Yin Jishan and Jiangsu Governor Chen Hongmou, and both men valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 初從武功孫景烈遊，講濂、洛、關、閩之學；

translations.literal: At first he associated with Sun Jinglie of Wugong and studied the learning of the Zhou, Luo, Guan, and Min schools;
translations.idiomatic: Early on he studied under Sun Jinglie of Wugong, taking up the Neo-Confucian traditions associated with Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi;

sentences.zh: 及見宏謀，學益進，自謂生平行己居官得力於此。

translations.literal: After meeting Hongmou his learning advanced further, and he said that his conduct in life and in office owed its strength to this.
translations.idiomatic: Once he came under Chen Hongmou's influence his learning deepened further, and he credited this training with whatever strength he showed in personal conduct and public service.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十六年，成進士，殿試進呈卷列第三。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi; his palace examination paper submitted to the throne ranked third.
translations.idiomatic: In 1761 he passed the metropolitan examination and took his jinshi degree; the palace examination paper presented to the throne placed him third.

sentences.zh: 高宗熟視字體如素識，以昔為尹繼善繕疏，曾邀宸賞，詢知人品，即拔置第一。

translations.literal: Gaozong stared long at the handwriting as if he knew it; recalling that Jie had once copied memorials for Yin Jishan and had won imperial praise, he inquired into his character and immediately raised him to first place.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qianlong studied the script at length as though it were familiar, remembered that Jie had once drafted memorials for Yin Jishan to imperial acclaim, asked about his character, and at once promoted him to first place.

sentences.zh: 及引見，風度凝然，上益喜。

translations.literal: When he was presented, his bearing was composed and dignified, and the emperor was still more pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience his bearing was grave and steady, and the emperor was all the more delighted.

sentences.zh: 又以陝人入本朝百餘年無大魁者，時值西陲戡定，魁選適得西人，御製詩以紀其事。

translations.literal: Also, for more than a hundred years since the dynasty's founding no man from Shaanxi had won the top honor; as the western frontier had just been pacified and the top graduate happened to be a westerner, the emperor composed an imperial poem to record the event.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the century and more since the dynasty's rise no Shaanxi native had taken first place in the palace examination; with the western campaigns just concluded and the top honor falling by chance to a man from the west, the emperor wrote an imperial poem to commemorate it.

sentences.zh: 尋直南書房，屢司文柄。

translations.literal: Soon after he entered the Southern Study and repeatedly oversaw literary examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to the Southern Study and repeatedly put in charge of civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 五遷至內閣學士。

translations.literal: After five promotions he reached Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Five promotions later he had risen to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，授刑部侍郎，調吏部，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Punishments, transferred to Personnel, and promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In 1774 he was made vice minister of punishments, transferred to the Board of Personnel, and promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，丁母憂，即家擢兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, while mourning his mother, he was promoted from home to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In 1783, while at home in mourning for his mother, he was promoted to minister of war without returning to the capital.

sentences.zh: 車駕南巡，傑赴行在謝，上曰：「汝來甚好。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured the south, Jie went to the temporary residence to pay thanks; the emperor said, "Your coming is very good.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern tour Jie came to the temporary palace to express his gratitude; the emperor said, "It is very good that you have come.

sentences.zh: 君臣久別，應知朕念汝。

translations.literal: Monarch and subject have been apart long; you ought to know that I miss you.
translations.idiomatic: Monarch and subject have been long parted—you should know that I have been thinking of you.

sentences.zh: 然汝儒者，不欲奪汝情，歸終制可也。

translations.literal: Yet you are a Confucian scholar; I do not wish to deprive you of your feelings—return and complete your mourning period."
translations.idiomatic: But you are a scholar; I do not wish to tear you from your filial duty—go home and finish your mourning."

sentences.zh: 」服闋，還朝。

translations.literal: When the mourning ended, he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning was complete, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，命為軍機大臣、上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he was appointed Grand Councilor and Chief Tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In 1786 he was appointed a grand councilor and chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 次年，拜東閣大學士，管理禮部。

translations.literal: The following year he was made Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and put in charge of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and given charge of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 台灣、廓爾喀先後平，兩次圖形紫光閣，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Taiwan and Gurkha were pacified in succession; twice his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Glaze, and he was given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the successive pacification of Taiwan and the Gurkhas, his portrait was twice placed in the Hall of Purple Glaze, and he received the additional title of grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 傑在樞廷十餘年，事有可否，未嘗不委曲陳奏。

translations.literal: Jie was in the Grand Council for more than ten years; whenever a matter could be approved or rejected, he never failed to set it forth tactfully in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Jie served on the Grand Council for more than ten years; on every matter that admitted approval or objection, he invariably laid out his views with careful tact in memorial.

sentences.zh: 和珅勢方赫，事多擅決，同列隱忍不言，傑遇有不可，輒力爭。

translations.literal: Heshen's power was then at its height and he decided many matters on his own; his colleagues endured in silence, but whenever Jie found something unacceptable he would contend vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen's influence was then at its zenith and he often decided affairs on his own; his colleagues swallowed their objections, but whenever Jie found a matter unacceptable he would argue it out.

sentences.zh: 上知之深，和珅雖厭之而不能去。

translations.literal: The emperor knew this deeply; though Heshen disliked him, he could not remove him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood this well; though Heshen resented him, he could not drive him out.

sentences.zh: 傑每議政畢，默然獨坐。

translations.literal: After each policy discussion Jie would sit alone in silence.
translations.idiomatic: After each council session Jie would sit apart in silence.

sentences.zh: 一日，和珅執其手戲曰：「何柔荑乃爾！

translations.literal: One day Heshen took his hand jestingly and said, "How soft and delicate!
translations.idiomatic: One day Heshen seized his hand in jest and said, "What delicate hands these are!

sentences.zh: 」傑正色曰：「王杰手雖好，但不能要錢耳！

translations.literal: " Jie said sternly, "Though Wang Jie's hand is fair, it cannot take money!"
translations.idiomatic: " Jie replied gravely, "Wang Jie's hands may be fair, but they cannot take bribes!"

sentences.zh: 」和珅赧然。

translations.literal: " Heshen blushed.
translations.idiomatic: " Heshen flushed with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，以足疾乞免軍機、書房及管理部事，允之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, citing foot ailment he begged to be relieved of Grand Council duty, the study, and ministerial administration; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1796, pleading foot trouble, he asked to be excused from the Grand Council, the study, and his ministerial duties; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 有大事，上必諮詢，傑亦不時入告。

translations.literal: When great matters arose the emperor always consulted him, and Jie also reported in from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: On weighty affairs the emperor still sought his counsel, and Jie would also come in from time to time to report.

sentences.zh: 時教匪方熾，傑疏言：「賊匪剿滅稽遲，由被賊災民窮無倚賴，地方官不能勞來安輯，以致脅從日眾，兵力日單而賊焰日熾。

translations.literal: At that time the sect rebels were raging fiercely; Jie memorialized: "The delay in suppressing the bandits is because victims of the rebels, impoverished and without support, are not comforted and settled by local officials, so that those forced to join grow daily in number, military strength daily weakens, and rebel flames daily mount.
translations.idiomatic: While the White Lotus rebels were at their height, Jie submitted a memorial: "The slow progress in wiping out the rebels stems from the fact that people ruined by the rebellion are destitute and without refuge, while local officials fail to relieve and settle them, so that those coerced into joining the rebels grow daily, the army grows thinner day by day, and rebel power burns brighter.

sentences.zh: 此時當安良民以解從賊之心，撫官兵以勵行間之氣。

translations.literal: At this time one should settle the good people to dissolve the heart to follow the rebels, and comfort the officers and soldiers to encourage morale in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture the government should reassure law-abiding people so as to loosen their attachment to the rebels, and care for the troops so as to raise fighting spirit in the field.

sentences.zh: 三年之內，川、楚、秦、豫四省殺傷不下數百萬，其倖存而不從賊者，亦皆鋒鏑之餘，男不暇耕，女不暇織。

translations.literal: Within three years in the four provinces of Sichuan, Huguang, Shaanxi, and Henan those killed and wounded were no fewer than several millions; even those who survived and did not join the rebels were all remnants after arms, men with no leisure to plow, women with no leisure to weave.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years in Sichuan, Huguang, Shaanxi, and Henan the dead and wounded numbered no less than several million; even survivors who had not joined the rebels were left shattered by war—men had no time to farm, women no time to weave.

sentences.zh: 若再計畝徵輸，甚至分外加派，胥吏因緣勒索，艱苦情形無由上達聖主之前。

translations.literal: If taxes are again levied by the mu and even extra assessments are imposed by quota, yamen runners seize the occasion to extort, and their bitter plight cannot reach the sage sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: If land tax is again assessed acre by acre, with surcharges piled on by quota, and clerks use the chance to squeeze them, their misery will never reach Your Majesty's ears.

sentences.zh: 祈將被賊地方錢糧蠲免，不令官吏舞弊重徵，有來歸者概勿窮治，賊勢或可漸孤矣。

translations.literal: I pray that grain and tax payments in rebel-afflicted regions be remitted, that officials not be allowed to cheat and levy heavily again, and that those who come back not be prosecuted to the end—then rebel strength may gradually be isolated.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that taxes and grain levies in rebel-ravaged districts be remitted, that officials be barred from fraudulent over-collection, and that deserters who return home be left unpunished—then the rebels may gradually be cut off.

sentences.zh: 至於用兵三載未即成功，實由將帥有所依恃，怠玩因循，非盡士卒之不用命也。

translations.literal: As for three years of campaigning without immediate success, it is really because generals have something to rely on and are slack and procrastinating—not wholly because the soldiers are disobedient.
translations.idiomatic: As for three years of war without decisive victory, the real cause is that commanders have patrons to shield them and grow slack and dilatory—it is not simply that the rank and file refuse to fight.

sentences.zh: 乞頒發諭旨，曲加憐恤，有驕惰不馴者，令經略概行撤回，或就近更調召募，申明紀律，鼓行勵戎，庶幾人有挾纊之歡，眾有成城之志。

translations.literal: I beg that an edict be issued showing special compassion; those who are arrogant, lazy, and unruly should be recalled wholesale by the commander-in-chief, or replaced and recruited nearby; discipline should be made clear and the army encouraged—then perhaps men will have the joy of wearing padded coats and the multitude the will to defend the walls together.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that an edict go forth showing them special kindness: let the commander-in-chief recall every arrogant, idle, or insubordinate officer, replace them with local recruits if need be, enforce discipline, and rouse the army—then the men may feel the comfort of a winter coat and the host the spirit to stand as one wall.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「教匪之蔓延，其弊有二：一由統領之有名無實。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The spread of the sect rebels has two abuses: first, the commander-in-chief is nominal without real authority.
translations.idiomatic: " He went on: "The rebels' spread has two root causes. First, the supreme commander holds a title without real command.

sentences.zh: 勒保雖為統領，而統兵大員名位相等，人人得專摺奏事，於是賊至則畏避不前，賊去則捏稱得勝。

translations.literal: Though Lebao was commander-in-chief, the great officers commanding troops were equal in rank and title, and each could submit memorials on his own; thus when rebels came they shrank back and would not advance, and when rebels left they fabricated claims of victory.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lebao was named commander-in-chief, the field generals were his equals in rank, and each could memorialize the throne on his own; when the rebels appeared they hung back in fear, and when the rebels withdrew they invented victories.

sentences.zh: 即如前歲賊竄興安，領兵大員有'匪已渡江五日，地方官並不禀報'之奏，此其畏避情形顯而易見。

translations.literal: For example, the year before last when rebels fled into Xing'an, a commanding officer memorialized that 'the bandits had crossed the river five days ago and local officials had not reported it'—their fear and evasion are obvious.
translations.idiomatic: Last year, for instance, when rebels broke into Xing'an, one field commander reported that the bandits had crossed the river five days earlier while local officials had not notified him—how plainly this shows their timidity and evasion.

sentences.zh: 又如去歲賊擾西安城南，殺傷數万，官兵既不近賊，撫臣一無設施；

translations.literal: Again, last year when rebels harried south of Xi'an city, tens of thousands were killed and wounded; the officers and soldiers did not approach the rebels, and the governor undertook nothing;
translations.idiomatic: Again, last year when rebels ravaged the country south of Xi'an, tens of thousands were killed or wounded; the troops never closed with the enemy, and the provincial governor did nothing at all;

sentences.zh: 探知賊去已遠，然後虛張聲勢，名為追賊，實未見賊。

translations.literal: after learning the rebels were already far away they then made a false show of force, called it pursuing the rebels, but in fact never saw the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: only after scouts reported the rebels far away did they raise a great clamor in the name of pursuit, though in truth they never sighted the enemy.

sentences.zh: 近聞張漢潮蔓延商、雒，高均德屯據洋縣，往來衝突，如入無人之境。

translations.literal: Recently it is heard that Zhang Hanchao spreads through Shang and Luo, Gao Junde occupies Yang County, and they clash back and forth as if entering a land without men.
translations.idiomatic: Lately Zhang Hanchao has spread through Shangzhou and Luozhou, while Gao Junde holds Yang County; they strike back and forth as though no one stood in their way.

sentences.zh: 秦省如此，川省可知。

translations.literal: If Shaanxi is thus, Sichuan may be known.
translations.idiomatic: If Shaanxi is in this state, one can imagine what Sichuan must be like.

sentences.zh: 實由統領不專、賞罰不明之所致也。

translations.literal: It is really caused by the commander-in-chief lacking sole authority and rewards and punishments being unclear.
translations.idiomatic: This truly comes of a commander without sole authority and of rewards and punishments left unclear.

sentences.zh: 一由領兵大員專恃鄉勇。

translations.literal: Second, commanding officers rely solely on local militia.
translations.idiomatic: Second, field commanders rely exclusively on local militia.

sentences.zh: 鄉勇陣亡，無庸報部，人數可以虛捏；

translations.literal: When militia die in battle there is no need to report to the ministry, and numbers can be falsely inflated;
translations.idiomatic: Militia casualties need not be reported to the Board of War, so head counts can be invented;

sentences.zh: 藉鄉勇為前陣，既可免官兵之傷亡，又可為異日之開銷，此所以耗國帑而無可稽核也。

translations.literal: using militia as the front line both spares regular troops from casualties and provides future expenses—this is why the state treasury is drained with nothing to audit.
translations.idiomatic: using militia as the vanguard both keeps regular troops out of harm's way and pads future expense accounts—hence the treasury bleeds dry with nothing to audit.

sentences.zh: 臣以為軍務緊要，莫急於去鄉勇之名而為召募之實，蓋有五利：一，民窮無依，多半從賊，苟延性命，募而為兵，即有口糧，多一為兵之人，即少一從賊之人；

translations.literal: Your servant holds that in military affairs nothing is more urgent than abolishing the name of militia and making real recruitment; there are five benefits: first, the people are poor and without support and mostly follow the rebels to prolong life—recruit them as soldiers and they have rations; one more man as soldier is one fewer man following the rebels;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that in the present crisis nothing is more urgent than to end the militia fiction and recruit real soldiers. There are five advantages. First, the destitute, with nowhere to turn, mostly join the rebels merely to survive; recruit them as soldiers and they receive rations—every man enlisted is one fewer rebel.

sentences.zh: 一，隔省徵調，曠日持久，就近召募，則旬日可得；

translations.literal: second, calling troops from other provinces takes many days, while local recruitment can be obtained in ten days;
translations.idiomatic: Second, troops summoned from distant provinces take months to arrive, whereas local recruits can be raised in ten days;

sentences.zh: 一，徵兵遠來，筋力已疲，召募之人，不須跋涉；

translations.literal: third, conscripts coming from afar are already weary in sinew and strength, while recruited men need not trek long distances;
translations.idiomatic: Third, conscripts marched in from afar arrive exhausted, while local recruits need make no long march;

sentences.zh: 一，隔省之兵，水土不習，路徑不諳，就近之人，則不慮此；

translations.literal: fourth, troops from other provinces are unaccustomed to climate and water and do not know the roads, while local men need not fear this;
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, out-of-province soldiers are unaccustomed to climate and terrain and ignorant of the roads, whereas local men face no such handicap;

sentences.zh: 一，鄉勇勢不能敵，則逃散無從懲治，召募之兵退避，則有軍法。

translations.literal: fifth, when militia cannot match the enemy they scatter and flee with no means of punishment, but when recruited soldiers retreat there is military law.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, when militia cannot stand against the enemy they scatter without penalty, but regular recruits who flee can be punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 具此五利，何不增募，一鼓而殲賊？

translations.literal: With these five benefits, why not increase recruitment and destroy the rebels in one stroke?
translations.idiomatic: With these five advantages in view, why not expand recruitment and crush the rebels at a blow?

sentences.zh: 如謂兵多費多，獨不思一萬兵食十月之糧，與十萬兵食一月之糧，其費相等而功可早奏也。

translations.literal: If one says more troops mean more expense, has one not considered that ten thousand troops eating ten months' grain and one hundred thousand troops eating one month's grain cost the same, yet success can be reported earlier?
translations.idiomatic: If the objection is that more troops mean more expense, consider that ten thousand men fed for ten months and one hundred thousand men fed for one month cost the same, yet victory may be won far sooner.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，並被採用。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, its proposals were all adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial reached the throne, its recommendations were all adopted.

sentences.zh: 二年，復召直軍機，隨扈熱河。

translations.literal: In the second year he was again summoned to regular duty on the Grand Council and accompanied the emperor to Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: In 1797 he was recalled to regular Grand Council duty and accompanied the court to Rehe.

sentences.zh: 未幾，因腿疾，詔毋庸入直，先行回京。

translations.literal: Before long, because of leg ailment, an edict said he need not enter regular duty and he returned first to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on account of leg trouble, an edict excused him from regular attendance and he went back to Beijing ahead of the court.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，川匪王三槐就擒，封賞樞臣，詔：「傑現雖未直軍機，軍興曾有贊畫功，並予優敘。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year the Sichuan rebel Wang Sanhuai was captured; the Grand Councilors were enfeoffed and rewarded; an edict said: "Though Jie is not now on regular Grand Council duty, at the outbreak of war he had merit in planning and is also to receive preferential reward.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 1798 the Sichuan rebel Wang Sanhuai was captured; the grand councilors were ennobled and rewarded. An edict read: "Although Jie is not now on regular council duty, he rendered planning service when the war began and shall receive preferential recognition as well.

sentences.zh: 洎仁宗親政，傑為首輔，遇事持大體，竭誠進諫，上優禮之。

translations.literal: When Renzong took personal rule, Jie was chief minister; in affairs he held to the larger pattern, admonished with full sincerity, and the emperor treated him with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jiaqing Emperor took personal rule, Jie became chief minister; he kept to broad principle in state affairs, remonstrated with wholehearted sincerity, and the emperor honored him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 五年，以衰病乞休，溫詔慰留，許扶杖入朝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, citing age and illness he begged to retire; a warm edict comforted him and kept him on, allowing him to attend court leaning on a staff.
translations.idiomatic: In 1800, pleading age and infirmity, he asked to retire; a gracious edict urged him to stay and permitted him to attend court with a walking staff.

sentences.zh: 七年，固請致仕，晉太子太傅，在籍食俸。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he firmly begged to leave office; he was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and received salary while at home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802 he pressed his request to retire; he was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent and granted salary while living at home.

sentences.zh: 八年春，瀕行上疏，略謂：「各省虧空之弊，起於乾隆四十年以後，州縣營求餽送，以國帑為夤緣，上司受其挾制，彌補無期。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, on the eve of departure he submitted a memorial saying in summary: "The abuse of deficits in every province began after the fortieth year of Qianlong; districts and counties sought gifts and presents, used state funds as a ladder of connection, and superiors were constrained by them, with no end to making up deficits.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1803, on the eve of his departure, he submitted a farewell memorial stating in essence: "Provincial deficits began after 1775, when magistrates scrambled for gifts and used the public purse to buy favor; their superiors were held hostage to them, and the holes could never be filled.

sentences.zh: 至嘉慶四年以後，大吏知尚廉節，州縣仍形拮据，由於苦樂不均，賢否不分，宜求整飭之法。

translations.literal: After the fourth year of Jiaqing great officials knew to value integrity, yet districts and counties still appeared strained, because hardship and ease were uneven and the worthy and unworthy were not distinguished—methods of rectification should be sought.
translations.idiomatic: After 1799 the high officials learned to prize integrity, yet the magistrates remained hard pressed, because hardship and ease were unevenly shared and the capable were not distinguished from the corrupt—remedies for this must be found.

sentences.zh: 又，舊制，驛丞專司驛站，無可誅求。

translations.literal: Again, under the old system post station commissioners were solely in charge of stations and had nothing to extort.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, under the old system post commissioners managed the stations alone and had no opportunity for extortion.

sentences.zh: 自裁歸州縣，濫支苛派，官民俱病。

translations.literal: Since the posts were abolished and returned to districts and counties, reckless spending and harsh levies afflict both officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Since those posts were abolished and their duties folded into the magistracies, reckless spending and harsh levies have afflicted officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 宜先清驛站，以杜虧空。

translations.literal: The post stations should first be cleared up to stop deficits.
translations.idiomatic: The post system should be put in order first, as the surest way to stop the deficits.

sentences.zh: 今當軍務告竣，朝廷勤求治理，無大於此二者。

translations.literal: Now that military affairs are concluded, the court diligently seeks good government, and nothing is greater than these two matters.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the war is over and the court is earnestly seeking good government, nothing matters more than these two reforms.

sentences.zh: 請睿裁獨斷，以挽積重之勢。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty's wise decision acting alone to turn back this long-accumulated trend.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to decide these matters yourself and turn back this deeply entrenched decline.

sentences.zh: 」所言切中時弊，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: " What he said struck the abuses of the time; the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " His words went straight to the abuses of the day, and the emperor commended and accepted them.

sentences.zh: 陛辭日，賜高宗御用玉鳩杖、御製詩二章，以寵其行，有云：「直道一身立廊廟，清風兩袖返韓城。

translations.literal: On the day of his farewell audience he was given Gaozong's personal jade dove staff and two chapters of imperial verse to honor his departure, including the lines: "With upright conduct he stood alone in the hall of state; with clear breeze in both sleeves he returns to Hancheng."
translations.idiomatic: On the day he took leave of the throne he received the jade dove staff Qianlong had used in person and two imperial poems to honor his departure, including the lines: "Upright in office he stood alone in the hall of state; with empty sleeves and a clear name he returns to Hancheng."

sentences.zh: 」時論謂足盡其生平。

translations.literal: " Contemporary opinion said this fully summed up his life.
translations.idiomatic: " Contemporary opinion held that these lines summed up his life.

sentences.zh: 既歸，歲時頒賞不絕，每有陳奏，上輒親批答，語如家人。

translations.literal: After he returned, seasonal gifts and rewards never ceased; whenever he memorialized, the emperor personally wrote replies in language like family.
translations.idiomatic: After his return home, seasonal gifts from the court never ceased; whenever he wrote in, the emperor answered in his own hand in tones as familiar as family speech.

sentences.zh: 九年，傑與妻程並年八十，命巡撫方維甸齎御​​製詩、額、珍物，於生日就賜其家。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Jie and his wife Lady Cheng were both eighty; the emperor ordered Governor Fang Weidian to carry imperial verse, a plaque, and precious objects and bestow them at their home on their birthday.
translations.idiomatic: In 1804 Jie and his wife, née Cheng, both turned eighty; the emperor ordered Governor Fang Weidian to bring imperial poems, a commemorative plaque, and precious gifts and present them at their home on their birthday.

sentences.zh: 傑詣闕謝，明年正月，卒於京邸。

translations.literal: Jie went to the palace to give thanks; in the first month of the following year he died at his Beijing residence.
translations.idiomatic: Jie came to the capital to express his thanks; in the first month of the following year he died at his Beijing residence.

sentences.zh: 上悼惜，賜金治喪，贈太子太師，祀賢良祠，諡文端。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him with regret, granted gold for the funeral, posthumously made him Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and gave the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved his loss, granted gold for the funeral, posthumously appointed him grand preceptor of the heir apparent, had him enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and gave him the posthumous title Wenduan (Cultured and Upright).

sentences.zh: 傑體不逾中人，和靄近情，而持守剛正，歷事兩朝，以忠直結主知。

translations.literal: Jie's stature did not exceed that of an average man; he was kindly and approachable, yet held firm to integrity; serving two reigns, he won the sovereign's trust through loyalty and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was no taller than an average man, affable and warm in manner, yet unyielding in principle; serving two emperors, he won their trust through loyal, forthright service.

sentences.zh: 當致仕未行，會有陳德於禁城驚犯乘輿，急趨朝請對曰：「德庖廚賤役，安敢妄蓄逆謀？

translations.literal: When he had retired but not yet departed, Chen De suddenly alarmed the imperial carriage in the Forbidden City; Jie hurried to court and begged an audience, saying: "De is a low kitchen servant—how dare he harbor rebellious designs?
translations.idiomatic: Though he had retired but not yet left the capital, Chen De suddenly attacked the imperial carriage within the Forbidden City. Jie rushed to court and begged an audience, saying: "Chen De is a low kitchen servant—how could he dare harbor treason on his own?

sentences.zh: 此必有元姦大憝主使行明張差之事，當除肘腋之患。

translations.literal: There must be a chief villain behind him directing the affair, as in the clear case of Zhang Cha—the trouble at one's armpit must be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Some great villain behind the scenes must be directing this, as in the notorious Zhang Cha affair—we must root out the danger at the emperor's very side."

sentences.zh: 」至十八年林清逆黨之變，上思其言，特賜祭焉。

translations.literal: " When in the eighteenth year the Lin Qing rebel faction rose, the emperor recalled his words and specially granted sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Lin Qing rebellion broke out in 1813, the emperor recalled his warning and ordered a special sacrifice in his honor.

sentences.zh: 孫篤，道光二年進士，歷編修、御史，出為汀州知府、廣東督糧道，署鹽運使。

translations.literal: His grandson Du became a jinshi in the second year of Daoguang, served as compiler and censor, and went out as prefect of Tingzhou, Guangdong grain-supply intendant, and acting salt controller.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Du took his jinshi degree in 1822, rose through compiler and censor, and served outside the capital as prefect of Tingzhou, Guangdong grain intendant, and acting salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時林則徐為按察使，治海防，甚倚之。

translations.literal: At that time Lin Zexu was provincial judicial commissioner managing coastal defense and relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lin Zexu was provincial judicial commissioner in charge of coastal defense and relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 募廣州遊手精壯者備守禦，以機敏稱。

translations.literal: He recruited sturdy idlers of Guangzhou for defense and was known for quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited able-bodied Guangzhou street men for coastal defense and was noted for his resourcefulness.

sentences.zh: 擢山東布政使，署巡撫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Shandong provincial treasurer and acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Shandong provincial treasurer and served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 失察家人、屬官受賂，連降罷職歸，襄理西安城工。

translations.literal: He failed to detect that his household and subordinate officials took bribes, was demoted repeatedly and dismissed, returned home, and assisted in the Xi'an city works.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for failing to detect bribery by his household and subordinates, was demoted and dismissed, returned home, and helped supervise the Xi'an city wall project.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈布政使銜。

translations.literal: He died and was given the rank title of provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the rank of provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 董誥，字蔗林，浙江富陽人，尚書邦達子。

translations.literal: Dong Gao, style name Zhelin, was a native of Fuyang in Zhejiang, son of Minister Dong Bada.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Gao, whose courtesy name was Zhelin, came from Fuyang in Zhejiang and was the son of Minister Dong Bada.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十八年進士，殿試進呈卷列第三，高宗因大臣子，改二甲第一。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong; his palace examination paper submitted to the throne ranked third, but Gaozong, because he was a minister's son, changed him to first in the second class.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in 1763; his palace examination paper ranked third, but because he was a minister's son Qianlong moved him to first place in the second class.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，即預修國史、三通、皇朝禮器圖。

translations.literal: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he at once took part in compiling the national history, the Three Comprehensive Works, and the Illustrated Rites Implements of the Dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he immediately joined work on the national history, the Three Comprehensive Works, and the Illustrated Rites Implements of the Dynasty.

sentences.zh: 散館，授編修。

translations.literal: When the Hanlin term ended he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his Hanlin probation he was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，命入懋勤殿寫金字經為皇太后祝嘏。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was ordered to enter the Hall of Cultivated Diligence to copy the golden-character sutra to pray for the empress dowager's longevity.
translations.idiomatic: In 1767 he was ordered to the Hall of Cultivated Diligence to copy the golden-letter sutra in celebration of the empress dowager's birthday.

sentences.zh: 次年，大考翰詹，因寫經未與試，特加一級。

translations.literal: The following year in the great examination of Hanlin and academicians, because he had been copying sutras and did not take the test, he was specially given one rank higher.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the triennial examination of Hanlin and academy officials, he was excused from testing because of the sutra work and was specially promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 尋擢中允，丁父憂。

translations.literal: Soon after he was promoted to middle secretary and mourned his father.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to middle secretary of the heir apparent, then entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，服闋，入直南書房。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, when mourning ended, he entered regular duty in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In 1771, when his mourning was complete, he was assigned to regular duty in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 初，邦達善畫，受高宗知。

translations.literal: At first Bada was skilled at painting and won Gaozong's notice.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Bada had been a skilled painter and had won Qianlong's favor.

sentences.zh: 誥承家學，繼為侍從，書畫亦被宸賞，尤以奉職恪勤為上所眷注。

translations.literal: Gao inherited the family art, continued as an attendant, and his calligraphy and painting also won imperial praise; above all, his dutiful and diligent service won the emperor's special regard.
translations.idiomatic: Gao inherited his father's art, continued as a court attendant, and his calligraphy and painting likewise won imperial praise; above all, the emperor favored him for his scrupulous diligence in office.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四十年，擢工部侍郎，調戶部，歷署吏、刑兩部侍郎，兼管樂部。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works, transferred to Revenue, and successively acted as Vice Minister of Personnel and Punishments while also overseeing the Board of Music.
translations.idiomatic: In 1775 he was made vice minister of works, transferred to revenue, served in turn as acting vice minister of personnel and punishments, and also oversaw the Board of Music.

sentences.zh: 充四庫館副總裁，接辦全書薈要，命輯滿洲源流考。

translations.literal: He served as deputy director of the Siku Pavilion, took over the Essentials of the Complete Library, and was ordered to compile the Study of Manchu Origins.
translations.idiomatic: He served as deputy director of the Siku Library project, took charge of the Essentials of the Complete Library, and was ordered to compile the Study of Manchu Origins.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，命為軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1779 he was appointed a grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，加太子少保，擢戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1787 he received the additional title of junior guardian of the heir apparent and was promoted to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 台灣、廓爾喀先後底定，並列功臣，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: When Taiwan and Gurkha were pacified in succession he was listed among meritorious officials and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Glaze.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwan and the Gurkhas were pacified in turn, he was named among the meritorious officials and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Glaze.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，授受禮成，詔硃珪來京，將畀以閣務，仁宗賀以詩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, when the succession rites were completed, an edict summoned Zhu Gui to the capital to be given grand secretariat duties; Renzong congratulated him with a poem.
translations.idiomatic: In 1796, when the succession rites were complete, an edict summoned Zhu Gui to the capital for a grand secretariat post; the Jiaqing Emperor congratulated him with a poem.

sentences.zh: 屬稿未竟，和珅取白高宗曰：「嗣皇帝欲市恩於師傅。

translations.literal: Before the draft was finished Heshen took it and said to Gaozong: "The heir apparent wishes to curry favor with his tutor."
translations.idiomatic: Before the draft was finished, Heshen took it to Qianlong and said, "The heir apparent means to curry favor with his tutor."

sentences.zh: 」高宗色動，顧誥曰：「汝在軍機、刑部久，是於律意云何？

translations.literal: " Gaozong's expression changed; turning to Gao he said: "You have long been on the Grand Council and in the Ministry of Punishments—what is your view of the law in this?"
translations.idiomatic: " Qianlong's expression changed. Turning to Gao he said, "You have long served on the Grand Council and at the Board of Punishments—what does the law say of this?"

sentences.zh: 」誥叩頭曰：「聖主無過言。

translations.literal: " Gao kowtowed and said: "The sage sovereign's words are without fault."
translations.idiomatic: " Gao kowtowed and said, "The sage sovereign's words are never in error."

sentences.zh: 」高宗默然良久，曰：「汝大臣也，善為朕輔導之。

translations.literal: " Gaozong was silent a long while and said: "You are a great minister—well guide him for Us."
translations.idiomatic: " Qianlong was silent a long while, then said, "You are a senior minister—guide him well for Us."

sentences.zh: 」乃以他事罷珪之召。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Zhu Gui's summons was cancelled on another pretext.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu Gui's summons was then cancelled on another pretext.

sentences.zh: 時大學士懸缺久，難其人。

translations.literal: At that time a grand secretary post had long been vacant and a suitable man was hard to find.
translations.idiomatic: A grand secretary post had long stood vacant, and no suitable appointee could be found.

sentences.zh: 高宗謂劉墉、紀昀、彭元瑞三人皆資深，墉遇事模棱，元瑞以不檢獲愆，昀讀書多而不明理，惟誥在直勤勉，超拜東閣大學士，明詔宣示，俾三人加愧勵焉。

translations.literal: Gaozong said Liu Yong, Ji Yun, and Peng Yuanrui were all senior in service: Liu was evasive in affairs, Peng had been faulted for lack of restraint, Ji read much but did not understand principle—only Gao was diligent in regular duty, so he was promoted over them to Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, with an explicit edict to make the three feel ashamed and encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong said Liu Yong, Ji Yun, and Peng Yuanrui were all senior: Liu was evasive in office, Peng had been censured for misconduct, and Ji read widely but lacked sound judgment—only Gao was diligent in regular attendance. He was therefore promoted over them to grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, with an explicit edict meant to shame and spur the three.

sentences.zh: 命總理禮部，仍兼管戶部事。

translations.literal: He was ordered to oversee the Ministry of Rites while still managing Revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of the Ministry of Rites while continuing to oversee revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年，丁生母憂，特賜陀羅經被，遣御前侍衛、額駙丰紳殷德奠醊。

translations.literal: In the second year, mourning his birth mother, he was specially given a Buddhist sutra quilt and imperial guards including the emperor's son-in-law Fengshen Yinde were sent to offer libations.
translations.idiomatic: In 1797, while mourning his birth mother, he was specially granted a Buddhist sutra quilt, and imperial guards including the emperor's son-in-law Fengshen Yinde were sent to offer libations.

sentences.zh: 誥既以喪歸，川、楚兵事方亟，高宗欲召之，每見大臣，數問；

translations.literal: After Gao returned home for mourning, military affairs in Sichuan and Huguang were urgent; Gaozong wished to recall him and whenever he saw great ministers asked repeatedly,
translations.idiomatic: After Gao went home to mourn, the Sichuan and Huguang campaigns were pressing; Qianlong wished to recall him and whenever he met senior ministers asked repeatedly,

sentences.zh: 「董誥何時來？

translations.literal: "When will Dong Gao come?"
translations.idiomatic: "When will Dong Gao return?"

sentences.zh: 」逾年，葬母畢，詣京師，和珅遏不上聞。

translations.literal: " After a year, when his mother's burial was complete, he came to the capital; Heshen blocked report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: " A year later, when his mother's burial was finished, he came to Beijing, but Heshen prevented word from reaching the throne.

sentences.zh: 會駕出，誥於道旁謝恩，高宗見之，喜甚，命暫署刑部尚書，素服視事，不預典禮，專辦秋讞及軍營紀略，且曰：「誥守制已逾小祥，不得已用人之苦心，眾當共諒。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession went out, Gao thanked for grace by the roadside; Gaozong saw him and was greatly pleased, ordered him temporarily to act as Minister of Punishments, to handle affairs in plain mourning dress without attending ceremonies, specializing in autumn cases and military annals, and said: "Gao's mourning has passed the lesser anniversary—I use him from necessity of state; all should understand."
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession passed, Gao thanked him from the roadside. Qianlong saw him and was delighted, ordered him to act temporarily as minister of punishments, handle affairs in plain mourning garb without attending ceremonies, and focus on autumn judicial reviews and military chronicles, saying, "Gao's mourning has passed the lesser anniversary—I employ him from state necessity; all should understand."

sentences.zh: 」尋以王三槐就擒，與軍機大臣同被議敘。

translations.literal: " Soon when Wang Sanhuai was captured he received preferential reward along with Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon after Wang Sanhuai was captured, he received preferential recognition along with the grand councilors.

sentences.zh: 四年春，高宗崩，和珅伏誅，命誥复直軍機，晉太子太保。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year Gaozong died, Heshen was executed, and Gao was ordered back to regular Grand Council duty and promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1799 Qianlong died and Heshen was executed; Gao was restored to regular Grand Council duty and promoted to grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 既，服闋，授文華殿大學士，兼刑部尚書如故。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory while retaining Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory while retaining the ministry of punishments.

sentences.zh: 高宗山陵禮成，命題神主，晉太子太傅。

translations.literal: When Gaozong's mausoleum rites were completed he was ordered to compose the spirit tablet inscription and was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianlong's mausoleum rites were complete, he was ordered to compose the spirit-tablet inscription and was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 七年，三省教匪平，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the three provinces' sect rebels were pacified and he was given the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802, when the sect rebels in the three provinces were pacified, he was granted the hereditary rank of cavalry commandant.

sentences.zh: 十二年，高宗實錄告成，詔以誥在館八年，始終其事，特加優獎，賜其父邦達入祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year when Gaozong's veritable records were completed, an edict said that because Gao had been in the directorate eight years and saw the work through, he received special reward and his father Bada was given entry to the Shrine of Worthy Officials.
translations.idiomatic: In 1807, when Qianlong's veritable records were completed, an edict noted that Gao had spent eight years in the directorate and saw the project through; he received special reward, and his father Bada was admitted to the Shrine of Worthy Officials.

sentences.zh: 十四年，萬壽慶典，晉太子太師。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year at the longevity celebration he was promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1809, at the longevity celebration, he was promoted to grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: He was made Chief Tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 十七年，晉太保。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1812 he was promoted to grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 十八年，扈從秋狝。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he accompanied the autumn hunt.
translations.idiomatic: In 1813 he accompanied the autumn hunt at Mulan.

sentences.zh: 林清逆黨突入禁城，時回鑾，中途聞變，有議俟調大兵成列而後進者，誥曰：「是滋亂也，獻俘者行至矣！

translations.literal: Lin Qing's rebels broke into the Forbidden City; as they were returning mid-journey they heard of the disturbance; some advised waiting until great troops were assembled in formation before advancing; Gao said: "That would only stir disorder—the captives are already coming!"
translations.idiomatic: Lin Qing's rebels broke into the Forbidden City. The court was returning from the hunt and heard the news en route; some urged waiting until large forces were drawn up in formation before advancing. Gao said, "That would only spread panic—the men bringing captives are already on their way!"

sentences.zh: 」即日扈駕進次，人心乃定。

translations.literal: " That same day he accompanied the emperor to advance; public minds were calmed.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he accompanied the emperor forward, and public alarm subsided.

sentences.zh: 窮治邪教，誥謂：「燒香祈福，愚民無知，率所常有。

translations.literal: In thoroughly investigating the heterodox sect he said: "Burning incense to pray for blessings is something ignorant common people commonly do.
translations.idiomatic: In prosecuting the heterodox sects, Gao said, "Burning incense to pray for blessings is something ignorant common people commonly do.

sentences.zh: 惟從逆者不可貸。

translations.literal: Only those who followed the rebellion must not be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Only those who took part in the rebellion must not be spared."

sentences.zh: 」凡論上，皆以是定讞。

translations.literal: " In all sentencing memorials this standard was used to fix judgments.
translations.idiomatic: " In every sentencing recommendation this principle governed the final judgment.

sentences.zh: 林清既誅，滑縣逆匪尋平，論功，迭被優敘，賜子淳為郎中。

translations.literal: After Lin Qing was executed the Huaxian rebels were soon pacified; for merit he received repeated preferential rewards and his son Chun was given the rank of director.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin Qing was executed the Huaxian rebels were soon suppressed; for his merit he received repeated preferential rewards, and his son Chun was granted the rank of director.

sentences.zh: 二十年，因病請致政，溫詔慰留，改管兵部。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, ill, he begged to leave office; a warm edict kept him and changed his charge to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In 1815, pleading illness, he asked to retire; a gracious edict urged him to remain and transferred his portfolio to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復命管刑部。

translations.literal: Before long he was again ordered to manage Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again put in charge of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，再疏乞休，許致仕食全俸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he again memorialized to retire and was permitted to leave office on full salary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1818 he memorialized again to retire and was permitted to leave office on full salary.

sentences.zh: 是年十月，卒，贈太傅。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year he died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year he died and was posthumously made grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 上親奠，入祀賢良祠，賜金治喪，御製詩輓之，嘉其父子歷事三朝，未嘗增置一畝之田、一椽之屋，命刻詩於墓，以彰忠藎。

translations.literal: The emperor personally offered libation, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, granted gold for the funeral, and composed an elegiac poem praising father and son for serving three reigns without adding an extra mu of field or a single beam of house, ordering the poem carved on the tomb to show their loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor offered libation in person, had him enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, granted gold for the funeral, and composed an elegiac poem praising father and son for serving three reigns without acquiring an extra mu of land or a single extra rafter of roof, ordering the poem carved on the tomb to honor their loyal service.

sentences.zh: 諡文恭。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wengong (Cultured and Respectful).

sentences.zh: 誥直軍機先後四十年，熟於朝章故事，有以諮者，無不悉。

translations.literal: Gao served on regular Grand Council duty for forty years altogether, thoroughly versed in court regulations and precedents; when consulted he knew all.
translations.idiomatic: Gao served on regular Grand Council duty for forty years in all, thoroughly versed in court regulations and precedent; whatever he was asked, he knew completely.

sentences.zh: 凡所獻納皆面陳，未嘗用奏牘。

translations.literal: Whatever he offered in advice he stated face to face and never used written memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he offered in counsel he stated face to face and never put in written memorials.

sentences.zh: 當和珅用事，與王杰支柱其間，獨居深念，行處幾失常度，卒贊仁宗殲除大憝。

translations.literal: When Heshen held power he and Wang Jie supported the government between them; alone he pondered deeply and at times nearly lost composure, but in the end helped Renzong destroy the great villain.
translations.idiomatic: While Heshen held power he and Wang Jie bore up the government between them; alone he brooded deeply and at times nearly lost his composure, yet in the end helped the Jiaqing Emperor destroy the great villain.

sentences.zh: 及林清之變，獨持鎮定，尤為時稱雲。

translations.literal: At the Lin Qing disturbance he alone kept calm, especially praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: At the Lin Qing disturbance he alone kept his composure, which contemporaries especially praised.

sentences.zh: 硃珪，字石君，順天大興人。

translations.literal: Zhu Gui, style name Shijun, was a native of Daxing in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gui, whose courtesy name was Shijun, came from Daxing in Shuntian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先世居蕭山，自父文炳始遷籍。

translations.literal: His ancestors lived in Xiaoshan; from his father Wenbing the family registry was transferred.
translations.idiomatic: His family had lived in Xiaoshan; his father Wenbing was the first to transfer their household registration.

sentences.zh: 文炳官盩厔知縣，曾受經於大學士硃軾。

translations.literal: Wenbing was magistrate of Zhouzhi and had received instruction from Grand Secretary Zhu Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing served as magistrate of Zhouzhi and had studied the classics under Grand Secretary Zhu Shi.

sentences.zh: 珪少傳軾學，與兄筠同鄉舉，並負時譽。

translations.literal: Gui in youth inherited Shi's learning; with his elder brother Yun he passed the provincial examination together and both enjoyed contemporary repute.
translations.idiomatic: Gui in youth inherited Shi's learning; he and his elder brother Yun passed the provincial examination together, and both enjoyed high repute.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年成進士，年甫十八，選庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi at only eighteen, was selected as Hanlin bachelor, and after probation was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1748 he took his jinshi degree at only eighteen, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and after completing his probation was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 數遇典禮，撰進文冊。

translations.literal: He frequently encountered ceremonial occasions and drafted memorial documents.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in many state ceremonies and drafted the memorial documents presented on those occasions.

sentences.zh: 高宗重其學行，累遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Gaozong valued his learning and conduct and repeatedly promoted him to reader of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong valued his learning and character and repeatedly promoted him to reader of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，出為福建糧驛道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he went out as Fujian grain and courier intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1760 he was posted as Fujian grain and courier intendant.

sentences.zh: 擢按察使，治獄平恕，以父憂去。

translations.literal: Promoted provincial judicial commissioner; in judging cases he was fair and lenient; he left on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial judicial commissioner, where he judged cases with fairness and leniency, then left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，補湖北按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was appointed Hubei provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1767 he was appointed Hubei provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會緬甸用兵，以部署驛務詳慎，被褒獎。

translations.literal: When Burma was at war his deployment of courier services was detailed and careful and he received praise.
translations.idiomatic: During the Burma campaign his careful organization of courier services won praise.

sentences.zh: 調山西，就遷布政使，署巡撫。

translations.literal: Transferred to Shanxi, then promoted provincial treasurer and acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Shanxi, he was soon promoted provincial treasurer and served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 疏請歸化、綏遠二城穀二萬餘石搭放兵糧，以省採買、免紅朽；

translations.literal: He memorialized to lend out more than twenty thousand dan of grain from Guihua and Suiyuan cities for military rations, saving purchase costs and avoiding rotten surplus;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to lend out more than twenty thousand dan of grain stored at Guihua and Suiyuan for military rations, saving purchase costs and preventing spoilage;

sentences.zh: 又免土默特蒙古私墾罪，以所墾牧地三千餘頃，許附近兵民認耕納租，歲六千餘兩，增官兵公費；

translations.literal: also pardoned the crime of private cultivation by Tumed Mongols and allowed nearby soldiers and people to claim and farm more than three thousand qing of the reclaimed pasture, paying yearly rent of more than six thousand taels to augment official expenses;
translations.idiomatic: also pardoned Tumed Mongols for unauthorized cultivation and allowed nearby soldiers and civilians to claim and farm more than three thousand qing of reclaimed pasture, paying more than six thousand taels in annual rent to augment official expenses;

sentences.zh: 又太僕寺牧地苦寒，改徵折色，以便民除弊；

translations.literal: also because the imperial stud pastures were bitterly cold, changed collection to cash payment for the people's convenience and to remove abuses;
translations.idiomatic: also, because the imperial stud pastures were bitterly cold, he changed collection to cash payment for the people's convenience and to remove abuses;

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: all were referred to ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: all were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 珪方正，為同僚所不便，按察使黃檢奏劾讀書廢事。

translations.literal: Gui was upright and inconvenient for colleagues; provincial judicial commissioner Huang Jian memorialized impeachment that he neglected duties through reading.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was upright and awkward for his colleagues; provincial judicial commissioner Huang Jian memorialized that he neglected his duties through excessive reading.

sentences.zh: 四十年，召入覲，改授侍講學士，直上書房，侍仁宗學。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year summoned to audience he was changed to expositor and entered the Upper Study directly to tutor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1775 he was summoned to audience, appointed expositor, and assigned directly to the Upper Study to tutor the future Jiaqing Emperor.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，典福建鄉試。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he presided over the Fujian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1779 he presided over the Fujian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 次年，督福建學政。

translations.literal: The following year he supervised Fujian education.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Fujian education intendant.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，上五箴於仁宗：曰養心，曰敬身，曰勤業，曰虛己，曰致誠。

translations.literal: On departure he presented five admonitions to Renzong: cultivate the mind, respect the person, diligence in duty, empty the self, and utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving he presented five admonitions to the heir apparent: cultivate the mind, respect the person, be diligent in duty, empty the self, and practice utmost sincerity.

sentences.zh: 仁宗力行之，後親政，嘗置左右。

translations.literal: Renzong practiced them earnestly; after taking personal rule he often kept them at hand.
translations.idiomatic: The future emperor practiced them earnestly; after taking personal rule he often kept them at hand.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，擢禮部侍郎，典江南鄉試，督浙江學政。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year promoted Vice Minister of Rites, presided over Jiangnan provincial examination, supervised Zhejiang education.
translations.idiomatic: In 1786 he was promoted to vice minister of rites, presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination, and supervised Zhejiang education.

sentences.zh: 還朝，調兵部。

translations.literal: Returning to court he was transferred to War.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，典會試。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1790 he presided over the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 出為安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: He went out as Anhui governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 皖北水災，馳驛往賑，攜僕數人，與村民同舟渡，賑宿州、泗州、碭山、靈壁、五河、盱眙餘災，輕者貸以糧種。

translations.literal: When northern Anhui suffered flood he rode post to relieve; with only a few servants he crossed in the same boat with villagers, relieved remaining disaster in Suzhou, Sizhou, Dangshan, Lingbi, Wuhe, and Xuyi, lighter cases receiving seed grain on loan.
translations.idiomatic: When northern Anhui was flooded he rode post haste to relieve the victims, taking only a few servants and crossing in the same boats as the villagers; he relieved lingering disaster in Suzhou, Sizhou, Dangshan, Lingbi, Wuhe, and Xuyi, lending seed grain to the less severely affected.

sentences.zh: 築決堤，展春賑，並躬蒞其事，民無流亡。

translations.literal: He built broken dikes and extended spring relief, personally attending; the people had no exodus.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired breached dikes, extended spring relief, and personally oversaw the work, so that the people did not flee.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，調廣東。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1794 he was transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 尋署兩廣總督，授左都御史、兵部尚書，仍留巡撫任。

translations.literal: Soon he acted Liangguang Governor-General, was appointed left censor-in-chief and Minister of War while retaining the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served as acting Liangguang governor-general, was appointed left censor-in-chief and minister of war, and retained the governorship.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，授總督，兼署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he was appointed governor while also acting governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In 1796 he was appointed governor-general while also acting as governor.

sentences.zh: 珪初以文學受知，洎出任疆寄，負時望，將大用。

translations.literal: Gui had first won notice through literature; when he went out to frontier duty he carried high expectation and was to be greatly used.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had first won notice through his scholarship; when he took up frontier duty he bore high expectations and seemed destined for the highest office.

sentences.zh: 和珅忌之，授受禮成，珪進頌冊，因加指摘，高宗曰：「陳善納誨，師傅之職宜爾，非汝所知也。

translations.literal: Heshen envied him; when succession rites were completed Gui presented a eulogy scroll and Heshen seized the chance to criticize; Gaozong said: "To present good counsel and accept remonstrance is a tutor's proper duty—not something you understand."
translations.idiomatic: Heshen envied him. When the succession rites were complete, Gui presented a congratulatory scroll, and Heshen seized the chance to criticize him. Qianlong said, "To offer good counsel and accept remonstrance is a tutor's proper duty—not something you would understand."

sentences.zh: 」會大學士缺，詔召珪，卒為和珅所沮。

translations.literal: " When a grand secretary post became vacant an edict summoned Gui but Heshen blocked it in the end.
translations.idiomatic: " When a grand secretary post fell vacant, an edict summoned Gui, but Heshen blocked the appointment in the end.

sentences.zh: 以廣東艇匪擾劫閩、浙，責珪不能緝捕，寢前命，左遷安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: Because Guangdong boat bandits harassed Fujian and Zhejiang, Gui was blamed for failing to capture them, the earlier order was shelved, and he was demoted to Anhui governor.
translations.idiomatic: Because Guangdong boat bandits raided Fujian and Zhejiang, Gui was blamed for failing to capture them; the earlier appointment was shelved, and he was demoted to governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 皖北复災，親治賑，官吏無侵蝕。

translations.literal: Northern Anhui again suffered disaster; he personally managed relief and officials did not embezzle.
translations.idiomatic: When northern Anhui was flooded again, he personally managed relief, and officials did not embezzle funds.

sentences.zh: 三省教匪起，安徽亦多伏莽。

translations.literal: When sect rebels rose in three provinces Anhui also had many hidden bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When sect rebels rose in three provinces, Anhui also harbored many hidden bandits.

sentences.zh: 珪曰：「疑而索之，是激之變。

translations.literal: Gui said: "To suspect and search for them is to provoke rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "To suspect people and hunt them down is to provoke rebellion."

sentences.zh: 」親駐界上籌防禦，遍蒞潁、亳所屬，集鄉老教誡之，民感化，境內迄無事。

translations.literal: " He personally stationed on the border to plan defense, went everywhere in Ying and Bo districts, gathered village elders to instruct them, and the people were transformed; within the province there was no incident.
translations.idiomatic: " He personally stationed on the border to plan defense, toured every district under Yingzhou and Bozhou, gathered village elders to instruct them, and the people were won over; within the province there was no trouble.

sentences.zh: 明年，授兵部尚書，調吏部，仍留巡撫任。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Minister of War, transferred to Personnel, still retaining the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed minister of war, transferred to the Board of Personnel, and retained the governorship.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，高宗崩，仁宗即馳驛召珪，聞命奔赴。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year Gaozong died; Renzong immediately sent post to summon Gui, who hurried on receiving the order.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1799 Qianlong died; the Jiaqing Emperor immediately sent post to summon Gui, who hurried to the capital on receiving the order.

sentences.zh: 途中上疏，略曰：「天子之孝，以繼志述事為大。

translations.literal: En route he memorialized saying in summary: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety lies chiefly in continuing the late emperor's will and carrying forward his work.
translations.idiomatic: En route he submitted a memorial stating in essence: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety consists chiefly in continuing the late emperor's will and carrying forward his work.

sentences.zh: 親政伊始，遠聽近瞻，默運乾綱，雱施渙號。

translations.literal: At the start of personal rule, listen far and near, silently wield the imperial handle, and broadly issue sustaining edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of your personal rule, listen far and near, silently wield the imperial authority, and issue broad, sustaining edicts.

sentences.zh: 陽剛之氣，如日重光，惻怛之仁，無幽不浹。

translations.literal: The yang force, like the sun redoubled in light; compassionate benevolence penetrating everywhere without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Let your yang force shine like the sun redoubled in light; let compassionate benevolence reach every hidden corner.

sentences.zh: 修身則嚴誠欺之界，觀人則辨義利之防。

translations.literal: In self-cultivation draw a strict line against deception; in viewing men distinguish the boundary between righteousness and profit.
translations.idiomatic: In self-cultivation draw a strict line against deceit; in judging men distinguish the boundary between righteousness and profit.

sentences.zh: 君心正而四維張，朝廷清而九牧肅。

translations.literal: When the ruler's mind is correct the four pillars stand firm; when the court is pure the nine regions are orderly.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler's mind is upright the four pillars of state stand firm; when the court is pure the nine provinces are orderly.

sentences.zh: 身先節儉，崇獎清廉，自然盜賊不足平，財用不足阜。

translations.literal: Take the lead in frugality and honor clean officials—then bandits need not be fully suppressed and revenues need not be fully augmented.
translations.idiomatic: Take the lead in frugality and honor upright officials, and bandits will be subdued and revenues enriched without extraordinary effort.

sentences.zh: 惟原皇上無忘堯、舜自​​任之心，臣敢不勉行義事君之道。

translations.literal: Only pray the emperor not forget the heart that takes Yao and Shun upon himself; your servant dares not fail to strive to practice righteous service to the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Only pray Your Majesty never forget the resolve to measure yourself against Yao and Shun; your servant dares not fail to practice righteous service to the throne."

sentences.zh: 」至京哭臨，上執珪手哭失聲。

translations.literal: " Arriving at the capital for the mourning audience, the emperor took Gui's hand and wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: " At the capital mourning audience the emperor took Gui's hand and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 命直南書房，管戶部三庫，加太子少保，賜第西華門外。

translations.literal: He was ordered to regular duty in the Southern Study, manage the three treasuries of Revenue, given Junior Guardian title and a residence outside Xihua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to regular duty in the Southern Study, put in charge of the three revenue treasuries, granted the title of junior guardian of the heir apparent, and given a residence outside Xihua Gate.

sentences.zh: 時召獨對，用人行政悉以諮之。

translations.literal: Often summoned for private audience; appointments and administration were all consulted with him.
translations.idiomatic: He was often summoned for private audiences; appointments and administration were all referred to him.

sentences.zh: 珪造膝密陳，不關白軍機大臣，不沽恩市直，上傾心一聽，初政之美，多出贊助。

translations.literal: Gui spoke confidentially knee to knee, did not inform Grand Councilors, did not curry favor by direct appeal; the emperor listened with full trust; the beauty of early administration owed much to his support.
translations.idiomatic: Gui spoke confidentially at the emperor's knee, did not inform the grand councilors, and did not court favor by direct appeal; the emperor listened with full trust, and much of the excellence of the early reign owed to his counsel.

sentences.zh: 尋充上書房總師傅，調戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Chief Tutor of the Upper Study and transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made chief tutor of the Upper Study and transferred to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 詔清漕政，禁浮收​​。

translations.literal: An edict ordered cleaning grain transport administration and forbidding excessive collection.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered reform of grain transport administration and forbade excessive collection.

sentences.zh: 疆吏以運丁苦累，仰給州縣，州縣不得不取諸民，於是安徽加贈銀，江蘇加耗米，珪謂小民未見清漕之益，先受其害，力爭罷之，令曹司凡事近加賦者皆議駁。

translations.literal: Frontier officials said transport laborers suffered and depended on districts and counties, which had to levy on the people; thus Anhui added gift silver and Jiangsu added waste rice; Gui said common people had not yet seen benefit from clean transport but already felt harm first; he contended vigorously to abolish these and ordered all offices to reject nearby proposals to increase levies.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials said transport laborers were overburdened and depended on the districts and counties, which in turn had to levy on the people; Anhui therefore added gift silver and Jiangsu added waste-rice surcharges. Gui argued that the common people had not yet seen any benefit from transport reform but already felt the harm; he fought vigorously to abolish these levies and ordered every office to reject proposals for new surcharges.

sentences.zh: 長蘆鹽政請加增鹽價，駁曰：「蘆東因錢價賤，已三加價矣，且免積欠三百六十萬兩，餘欠展三年，商力已寬，無庸再議加價。

translations.literal: The Changlu salt administration asked to raise salt price again; he rejected: "East of the Pass because cash was cheap price was already raised three times, and three million six hundred thousand taels of arrears were remitted with remainder extended three years—merchants' resources are already eased; no need to discuss raising price again."
translations.idiomatic: The Changlu salt administration asked to raise the salt price again; he rejected it: "East of the Pass, because cash was cheap, the price has already been raised three times, and 3.6 million taels of arrears were remitted with the remainder extended three years—the merchants' resources are already eased; there is no need to discuss another price increase."

sentences.zh: 」廣東請濱海沙地升賦，駁曰：「海沙淤地，坍漲靡常，故照下則減半賦之。

translations.literal: " Guangdong asked to raise assessment on coastal reclaimed land; he rejected: "Sea-silt land shifts with accretion and erosion, so it is assessed at half the lower rate."
translations.idiomatic: " Guangdong asked to raise the land tax on coastal reclaimed fields; he rejected it: "Sea-silt land shifts with erosion and accretion, so it is assessed at half the lower rate."

sentences.zh: 今視上、中田增賦，是與民計微利，非政體。

translations.literal: " Now to raise assessment like upper and middle fields is to scheme petty profit against the people, not proper government."
translations.idiomatic: " To raise the assessment to the level of upper and middle-grade fields is to squeeze petty profit from the people, not sound government."

sentences.zh: 且民苦加賦，別有漲地，將不敢報墾，不可行。

translations.literal: " Moreover the people suffer from increased levies; if there is other reclaimed land they will not dare report cultivation—this cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: " Moreover, the people already suffer from higher levies; if other reclaimed land exists, they will not dare report it for taxation—this must not be done."

sentences.zh: 」倉場請預納錢糧四五十倍，準作義監生，駁曰：「國家正供有常經，名實關體要。

translations.literal: " The granary administration asked to prepay grain tax forty or fifty times over and qualify as charitable student; he rejected: "State regular payments have fixed rules; name and reality concern fundamentals of government.
translations.idiomatic: " The granary administration asked that grain tax be prepaid forty or fifty times over in exchange for charitable-student status; he rejected it: "The state's regular revenues follow fixed rules; name and reality touch the foundations of government.

sentences.zh: 於名不正，實必傷，斷不可行。

translations.literal: If the name is not correct the reality must be harmed—absolutely cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: If the name is not correct, the reality must suffer—this absolutely cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 」凡駁議每自屬稿，奏上，皆韙之。

translations.literal: " In all rejections he usually drafted the memorial himself; when submitted the emperor approved them.
translations.idiomatic: " He usually drafted these rejections himself; when they were submitted, the emperor approved them all.

sentences.zh: 五年，兼署吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he also acted as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1800 he also served as acting minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 先是彭元瑞於西華門內墜馬，珪呼其輿入舁之，為御史週栻所劾。

translations.literal: Earlier Peng Yuanrui fell from his horse inside Xihua Gate; Gui called his sedan in to carry him, for which Censor Zhou Shi impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Peng Yuanrui fell from his horse inside Xihua Gate; Gui had his sedan brought in to carry him, for which Censor Zhou Shi impeached him.

sentences.zh: 尋有珪輿人毆傷禁門兵，忌者嗾護軍統領訐之。

translations.literal: Soon Gui's sedan bearers beat and injured forbidden-gate soldiers; enemies incited the guard commander to denounce him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gui's sedan bearers beat and injured gate guards; his enemies incited the guard commander to denounce him.

sentences.zh: 詔：「珪素恪謹，造次不檢，特申戒。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Gui is always careful and respectful; in a moment of carelessness he was not restrained—specially admonished."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Gui is always careful and respectful; in a moment of carelessness he was not restrained—he is specially admonished."

sentences.zh: 」坐褫宮銜，解三庫事，鐫級留任。

translations.literal: " He was punished by stripping palace rank, relieved of the three treasuries, reduced in rank but kept in office.
translations.idiomatic: " He was stripped of his palace rank, relieved of the three treasuries, reduced in rank, but kept in office.

sentences.zh: 七年，協辦大學士，复太子少保。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he assisted as grand secretary and was again made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802 he was made assisting grand secretary and again received the title of junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋兼翰林院掌院學士，晉太子少傅。

translations.literal: Soon he also served as Hanlin Academy chancellor and was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and was promoted to junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 九年，上幸翰林院，聯句賜宴，御書「天祿儲才」額刻懸院中，以墨書賜珪家。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the emperor visited the Hanlin Academy, held a joint-verse banquet, and inscribed the plaque "Heaven's Blessing Stores Talent" to be carved and hung in the academy; ink writing was given to Gui's family.
translations.idiomatic: In 1804 the emperor visited the Hanlin Academy, held a joint-verse banquet, and inscribed the plaque "Heaven's Blessing Stores Talent" to be carved and hung in the academy; an ink copy was given to Gui's family.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜體仁閣大學士，管理工部。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was made Grand Secretary of the Tiren Pavilion and put in charge of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1805 he was made grand secretary of the Tiren Pavilion and put in charge of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 上以是命遵高宗諭，遣詣裕陵謝。

translations.literal: Because of this appointment, following Gaozong's instruction, the emperor sent him to the Yu Mausoleum to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Because this appointment followed Qianlong's instruction, the emperor sent him to the Yu Mausoleum to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，年七十六，以老乞休，溫詔慰留，賜玉鳩杖；

translations.literal: A year later, at seventy-six, he begged to retire on account of age; a warm edict kept him on and granted a jade dove staff;
translations.idiomatic: A year later, at seventy-six, he asked to retire on account of age; a gracious edict urged him to stay and granted him a jade dove staff;

sentences.zh: 命天寒，間二三日入直。

translations.literal: he was ordered that in cold weather he need enter regular duty only every two or three days.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered that in cold weather he need attend regular duty only every two or three days.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召對乾清宮，眩暈，扶歸第，數日卒。

translations.literal: Before long summoned to audience at the Palace of Heavenly Purity, he grew dizzy, was helped home, and died after several days.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to audience at the Palace of Heavenly Purity, grew dizzy, was helped home, and died a few days later.

sentences.zh: 上親奠，哭之慟。

translations.literal: The emperor personally offered libation and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor offered libation in person and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，祀賢良祠，賜金治喪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and granted gold for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand tutor, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and granted gold for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 詔：「珪自為師傅，凡所陳說，無非唐、虞、三代之言，稍涉時趨者不出諸口，啟沃至多。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Since Gui was tutor, whatever he stated was nothing but words of the age of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties; anything touching current fashion never left his mouth; his counsel was abundant.
